2 قزّح القِدْرَ , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. تَقْزِيحٌ; (S;) and ↓ قَزَحَهَا , (Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
قَزَحَ , (K,) [inf. n. قَزْحٌ, as indicated in the K;] [He put into the cooking-pot seeds for seasoning, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) called قِزْح. (Msb, K.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] قزّح كَلَامَهُ (tropical:) He seasoned [meaning he embellished] his speech, or language; syn. تَوْبَلَهُ. (TA in art. تبل.) تَقْزِيحُ الحَدِيثِ mans (tropical:) The embellishing of discourse (K, TA) without lying therein. (TA.) ―
-b3- قزّح أَصْلَ الشَّجَرَة, in copies of the K incorrectly ↓ قَزَحَ , without tesh-deed, (TA,) He made water upon (بَوَّلَ) the root, or stem, of the tree: (K, TA:) or he put urine at the root of the tree to render its fruit abundant. (JK.) ―
-b4- See also 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
